title: Adaptive KV reservoir: shear-driven compaction and prioritized spill tiers
author: Rajiv Menon
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and reactive spill storms continue to surface at tail latency under mixed batch/streaming workloads. Small-object churn (tens to low hundreds of bytes) creates many tiny free fragments that the allocator cannot efficiently reuse, causing spill bursts and I/O pressure. This PR introduces an 'adaptive reservoir' layer and a shear-driven compaction pass plus a prioritized spill-tier policy to smooth memory reclamation and reduce tail latency.

review_thread: Elena García (reviewer): Can you clarify how the reservoir interacts with existing slab reservations? Is this orthogonal to the slab allocator or does it replace any path?

Author (Rajiv): The reservoir is an overlay that sits above slabs: it tracks small-fragment pools and leases reclaim windows to the compactor. It does not change the slab layout; it simply surfaces candidate segments for coalescing without blocking fast-path allocations.
Marcus Lee (reviewer): The compaction worker looks potentially heavy for multi-tenant hosts — what are the CPU and lock guarantees?

Author: Compaction is sheared into many tiny CPU-friendly tasks limited by a per-host token bucket and tenant fairness slots. There are explicit CPU caps and a low-priority scheduling class so it won't compete with inference kernels. Added metrics for compaction CPU and throttled_count.
Priya Kapoor (reviewer): I saw a flaky unit failing in CI once; can you add a retry or stabilize the timing in that test?
Author: Replaced time.Sleep-based assertion with explicit event notification; triggered a CI re-run and the suite passed.
ci_checks: bench: collected new kv_simulator scripts (optional), no regressions
benchmarks_summary: Local cluster run (8x A100 simulated) using kv_simulator with mixed 70/30 streaming/batched requests: 95th tail token latency reduced by 18% compared to baseline; median latency unchanged; spill frequency (spike events >3x baseline) reduced from 7/day to 1/day in a 24h simulation. Memory utilization smoothed: peak memory variance decreased 27%.
rollout_plan: Start on dedicated staging fleet with reservoir.enabled=false, enable in canary mode for 2% traffic for 48h, monitor compaction_cpu, spill_count, tail_latency. If metrics stable, ramp to 25% over 24h then to 100% after 72h. Fail-open: compaction can be disabled dynamically and spill_tiers fall back to prior LRU policy.

release_notes: Add adaptive reservoir overlay to reduce small-fragment churn and smooth memory usage.
Introduce shear-driven incremental compactor to coalesce fragments with bounded CPU budget.
Add prioritized spill tiers to reduce I/O spike frequency and improve tail latency under mixed workloads.
notes: This PR focuses on stabilization and observability. Follow-ups planned: 1) integrate kernel prefetch hints into compactor to reduce page faults during coalescing, 2) extend reservoir heuristics to tenant-specific coldspot detection, 3) add amber alerting for compaction throttling.
